headline: Free MBTA fares for non-driving seniors open to enrollment Oct. 13
dek: Massachusetts residents age 75 and older who no longer drive will be able to apply for a pilot credential covering MBTA buses, subways, ferries and Commuter Rail.
body: Massachusetts will begin enrollment Oct. 13 for a pilot program giving residents age 75 and older who no longer drive free fares on MBTA buses, subways, ferries and Commuter Rail, state officials announced Sept. 23.

Participants must have a Massachusetts identification card rather than a driver's license. The MBTA and Registry of Motor Vehicles are partnering on the program, which is intended to help older residents keep traveling to appointments, services and family connections after giving up driving.

Eligible residents will be able to apply online beginning Oct. 13 or visit the Charlie Service Center at 296 Washington St. in Boston. People who apply in person can receive a temporary credential that day; a permanent credential will be mailed later, according to the state announcement.

Residents who do not already have a Massachusetts ID will need to obtain one through the RMV before applying. The pilot is part of a broader set of MBTA affordability changes announced by the Healey administration this year, including reduced Commuter Rail fares and expanded transfer options.
author: NorthEast News Desk
